planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun; Trippy Pink forms an upright, well-branched plant that is smothered in hot-pink flower spikes from summer into fall and draws heavy butterfly and pollinator traffic.

directions: Set out container plants in spring in average to lean, well-drained soil in full sun, where heat and good drainage keep the plant blooming heavily rather than growing leggy. Because flowers form on new wood, cut the whole plant back hard to 12-18 inches in late winter or very early spring to keep its upright, well-branched shape and maximize the hot-pink flower spikes through summer and fall. The dense bloom display is highly attractive to butterflies and other pollinators, and once established the shrub tolerates heat and drought with only occasional watering. Deadheading spent spikes can encourage additional rebloom in long growing seasons.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; Big Beauty carries large, intensely fragrant double white flowers over a naturally rounded evergreen form that needs little shaping.

directions: Plant in acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil, giving full sun in milder climates or part shade where summer afternoons run hot, since gardenias scorch in reflected heat. Big Beauty produces an unusually heavy flush of large, double, waxy white blooms with strong classic gardenia fragrance against dark green glossy foliage, and its naturally rounded habit holds that shape with minimal pruning. Feed with an acid-forming fertilizer in spring and keep soil evenly moist but not waterlogged, since both drought stress and soggy roots cause bud drop. The dense form and heavy bloom make it a strong choice for hedging, foundation plantings, or as a fragrant specimen near patios and entries.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; Violet Mist stays markedly more compact than older chaste tree selections while still reblooming in waves of blue-purple flowers from early summer until fall.

directions: Plant in average to lean, well-drained soil in full sun, where heat and dry conditions encourage the densest, most repeat bloom. Violet Mist throws up successive spikes of blue-purple flowers through the heat of summer into fall, drawing bees and butterflies, and its compact, rounded habit fits smaller borders and foundation plantings that older, larger chaste tree cultivars could not. Prune hard in late winter since flowers form on new growth, and skip supplemental watering once roots are established, as this selection is notably drought and heat tolerant. Good drainage is more important than soil fertility for keeping the plant tidy and floriferous.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; Queen Bee spreads wider than tall and opens lavender flower spikes in mid-June that rebloom through summer, making it a strong pollinator plant for hot, dry sites.

directions: Plant in average, well-drained soil in full sun, giving Queen Bee plenty of lateral room since its spread exceeds its height at maturity. Lavender flower spikes open in mid-June and continue reblooming through summer, consistently drawing bees and other pollinators to the garden. The shrub shows strong tolerance of heat, drought, and winter cold once established, and an annual hard pruning in late winter keeps the rounded form dense and encourages the heaviest new-wood flowering. Its wide, mounded habit works well as a long-blooming hedge or border anchor in hot summer climates.

planting.note: Plant balled-and-burlapped or container trees in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; Courageous opens highly fragrant lilac-pink blooms over maroon new growth and holds an upright, broad form well suited to specimen or group plantings.

directions: Plant young trees in spring in well-drained soil in full sun, siting them where their eventual broad, upright canopy has room to spread. In spring, strongly fragrant lilac-pink flowers emerge alongside maroon new growth, a combination that attracts pollinators before the foliage matures to a green-bronze that turns yellow-orange in fall. This selection is bred for extreme cold hardiness, performing reliably into USDA zone 2, and needs only light structural pruning in late winter to maintain its form. Established trees tolerate drought and a range of soil types, making them a durable choice for cold-climate landscapes.

planting.note: Plant balled-and-burlapped or container trees in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; Green Wall Spire grows in a tight, narrow column, making it useful for screening or lining a wall where a full-spreading crabapple will not fit.

directions: Plant young trees in spring in well-drained soil in full sun, spacing them closely for a narrow screen or allee since the habit stays columnar rather than spreading. Pink buds open to white spring flowers, followed by red fruit that persists into winter against bright green summer foliage that turns bronze in fall, giving multi-season interest along with winter bird forage. Give the tree minimal pruning beyond removing crossing or damaged branches, since its tight upright form develops naturally. Established trees are cold hardy and drought tolerant, making this a practical option for narrow side yards or property-line screening where space is limited.
